subject: Post-call: Acme integration & rate-limits / next steps

Subject: Post-call: Acme integration & rate-limits / next steps

Hi Tom / Kavita

Thanks again for the call earlier great to meet the Infra and Search teams. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before kickoff: 

Summary of the call:
- Primary use case: customer-facing semantic search + reranking for product recommendations (embedding + reranker pipeline).
- Traffic profile: peak 200 QPS search queries across multiple regions, typical request size ~1-2 short passages + reranker candidates.
- SLA target: p95 generation latency <150ms for embeddings & reranker scoring in the critical path.
- Concerns: rate limits, per-tenant quotas, idempotency for user actions that trigger expensive reranks.

Action items / next steps (proposed):
1) Engineering kickoff: set up a short integrated spike SDK auth + example env that demonstrates embeddings -> reranker flow. (Owners: Alex from Acme + Marissa from Redwood)
2) Auth & routing: confirm whether you will use per-tenant API keys or a service account routing via our private deployment. We can provide scoped API keys and route by tenant id.
3) Rate limiting & quotas: we'll run a small capacity test to map QPS to token / cost curves, then propose per-tenant quotas and burst policies.
4) Retries & idempotency: design recommendation below (we included our standard approach in the attached integration guide).
5) Schedule: propose Wed 3/31 10:00am PT for the spike session.

Short tech notes on retries/idempotency (see guide for full text):
- 429 handling: exponential backoff with jitter, capped at 32s; prefer client-side retry budgets to avoid cascading failures.
- Idempotency: include a client-generated request_id header (UUID v4) for any request that results in a state change or charges usage; Redwood will treat request_id to dedupe within a 5-minute window.
- Embeddings & rerankers: use batched embedding calls and asynchronous reranker scoring where possible; Redwood supports batch endpoints and response streaming for partial results.

I attached a short integration guide and a starter spreadsheet with tentative quotas. Please confirm the spike time (Wed 3/31 10am PT) and whether Alex can join the spike.

Thanks,
Ben

Ben thanks for the clear notes. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- We plan to use a per-tenant service account model (each customer mapped to a service account) rather than exposing tenant-level API keys. Can you confirm Redwood supports service-account scoped tokens and routing by header (x-acme-tenant-id) so we can keep network-level isolation?
- For reranker costs: we need to understand ordering guarantees if a retry happens, e.g., user clicks "refresh recommendations" triggers a rerank job that should not double-count if a client retries due to a 429. Is the request_id approach enough?

Alex will join the spike; Wed 3/31 10am PT works.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-03-26T09:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call: Acme integration & rate-limits / next steps

Tom

Quick answers: yes, Redwood supports service-account scoped tokens (we can mint short-lived JWTs tied to a service account and a tenant header). Routing by x-acme-tenant-id is supported in our private deployment; for hosted we recommend routing by a tenant header + model pin to ensure consistent placement.

On idempotency/deduping: the client-generated request_id is the standard approach and is what we recommend. A couple implementation notes: 
- The request_id must be globally unique per user action (UUID v4 is fine).
- Redwood persists seen request_ids for a short dedupe window (default 5 minutes, configurable). If we detect a duplicate request_id for the same operation we return the original response or a 200 with a dedupe indicator.
- For long-running reranker jobs we recommend: client submits an operation with request_id -> Redwood returns operation_id; client polls the operation endpoint (GET /v1/operations/:id) which is idempotent. Retries on the POST will return the same operation_id.

On counting/costing: duplicate POSTs deduped server-side will not be double-billed; retries that create multiple distinct operation_id will be billable. The dedupe behavior is documented in the attached guide.

I'll prep a short spike checklist and a small sandbox token for Alex to use.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

2) Rate limits: can you share an example policy we could test against (per-tenant baseline 50 QPS, burst to 200 for 30s)? How are 429s surfaced in the SDK (error codes, headers like Retry-After)?
3) Backoff guidance: recommended retry strategy for AI inference calls vs. metadata ops (e.g., creating datasets) do you recommend different caps?

Looking forward to the spike can you drop the sandbox token and the sample code?

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Alex quick reply and resources ahead of Wed spike: 

1) SDKs & samples:
- Node + Python SDKs both supported. Starter samples: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/tree/main/js and /py.
- I'll attach a minimal Node example that shows: batching embeddings, then streaming reranker scoring + handling partial results.

2) Example rate-limit policy (we can tune during the spike):
- Per-tenant baseline: 50 QPS (per-second token throttle), burst window: allow up to 200 QPS for 30s if available capacity; token-based deduction for embedding batches.
- 429s: returned with HTTP 429, body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","code":"rate_limit","retry_after":seconds}. SDK surfaces Retry-After header and a structured error with retryable=true.

3) Backoff guidance: 
- Short inference calls (stateless / idempotent reads like embeddings): exponential backoff with full jitter, base 100ms, max cap 5s, 5 retries.
- Long-running ops (job creation, dataset writes): prefer client-side polling and fewer retries on POSTs; use request_id for idempotency. Backoff cap 32s for polling.

4) Sandbox token & creds: Marissa will drop a scoped sandbox service account token for Alex ahead of the spike and a small sandbox capacity we can use to simulate 200 QPS.

Attaching: redwood-integration-guide-v1.pdf and a short node sample (attached as a stub). See attached.

Thanks,
Ben
